finding.claim: Unauthenticated path traversal in download handler allows arbitrary file read on the host via the f query parameter.
finding.source: GET /dl?f=... query parameter (files.go:12), served on :8082 with no auth (files.go:32, 34).
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13, response written at files.go:18.

trace.note: /dl routed to download with no middleware or auth guard.
Attacker-controlled f query parameter read and used unmodified.
filepath.Join concatenates then Clean resolves '..' lexically, so f=../../../../etc/passwd resolves to /etc/passwd.
File contents written back to the HTTP response.

finding.guards_checked: No authentication or authorization on route; filepath.Join does not confine result to root; no '..' rejection, no filepath.Rel/prefix check against root, no resolved-path check. The avatar handler (files.go:21-29) was checked and not reported because filepath.Base at line 22 strips directory components and ReadFile on a directory errors.

verdict.guard_found: none. Route /dl is registered directly at files.go:32 with no middleware. The f value is read unmodified at files.go:12 and joined to root at files.go:13 with filepath.Join, which Cleans lexically, so "../../../../etc/passwd" resolves to /etc/passwd. No '..' rejection, no filepath.Rel or prefix check against root, and the ReadFile error only leads to a 404 (files.go:14-16). The avatar handler's filepath.Base at files.go:22 does not apply to /dl.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: files.go:32 routes /dl with no auth, files.go:12 takes f unmodified, files.go:13 Joins and reads with no containment check, and files.go:18 returns the bytes, so an anonymous HTTP client can read any file the server process can read.
